transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you, thank you for fitting me in. 

Um... well, I guess I'm here because things have been pretty stressful lately, and I just want to make sure I'm handling everything the right way. I hope I explain this okay. It's... it's about my father's passing. 

Everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly, and I really don't want to upset my family or cause a fuss. But, well, I'm a systems analyst, so I look at data and discrepancies all day. And when I compare the timestamps on those files, and I see these missing attachments... and then certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I ask them politely about it... 

I don't want to sound unreasonable, but it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. I'm just trying to understand it all... does that make sense? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just want to know the truth.
Do you think it’s possible that you could be mistaken about someone hiding what happened to your father?

I mean, I really wish I was mistaken, Doctor. I truly do. I know how it sounds, and I hate causing any friction with my family. I hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or... or paranoid. 

I've tried so hard to just accept what they're saying. I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But... well, I do this for a living, you know? And when I actually sit down and compare the timestamps, and I see those missing attachments... and then the way certain people in the community just completely avoid my questions when I ask them... I just can't ignore it. 

I really try to see it from their side, but it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. I'm just trying to be thorough and figure it out. Is it wrong of me to want to look into that?
Do you think it’s possible that the records and emails are all correct, and that there may be no hidden wrongdoing?

I... I really want to say yes, Doctor. I know that's probably what I should think, and it would definitely make things easier for my family if I just agreed and let it go. I really do try to see it that way, because I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. 

But... I'm sorry, I hope I'm not frustrating you. It's just that when I sit down and actually compare the timestamps myself, and I see those missing attachments... and then, well, the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions when I bring it up... I just can't shake it. As much as I want to believe everything is fine, it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. 

I don't want to be difficult, I promise I don't. I just can't unsee the discrepancies in the data. Does that... does that make sense why I'm having such a hard time just accepting it?
Do you think it is possible that your father’s death happened exactly as the hospital and family have explained, with no hidden wrongdoing at all?

I... I know you're trying to help me see it from another angle, Dr. ____, and I really appreciate that. I do. I know I probably sound like a broken record, and I'm so sorry if I'm being stubborn. I don't want you to think I'm just looking for trouble where there isn't any.

I try to tell myself that maybe it did happen exactly the way they say. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and donation emails all line up perfectly. And I want to believe them, I really do. It would be so much easier. 

But... um... when I look at the actual data... the timestamps that don't match, those missing attachments... and just the way certain community members completely avoid my questions... I just... I can't let it go. I'm sorry, I know it's probably not what you want to hear, but it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

I hope you can understand why I'm struggling with this. Am I making any sense at all? I just want to do the right thing.
How certain are you, from 0 to 100, that someone hid the truth about your father’s death?

Um... a number. Gosh, I really don't want to sound completely unreasonable to you, Doctor. I know saying 100 percent sounds... well, it sounds like I'm not listening to reason, and I promise you I am trying to. I really don't want you to think I'm just being difficult or, you know, paranoid. I value your professional opinion so much. So, maybe... 99? 

I know we keep going over this, and I'm so sorry to sound like a broken record. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But... well, since I do this for a living, when I look at those timestamps, and the missing attachments, and then the way certain community members just completely avoid me when I ask about it... it just remains so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened to him. 

I'm really sorry, I know that's probably frustrating to hear me say again. I just want to be completely honest with you about where my head is at. Is it... is it okay that I'm still feeling this way?
Do you have any other strong suspicions that people are watching, following, or trying to harm you?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm, well, paranoid about people coming after me or anything like that. I know exactly how that would sound, and I don't want you to worry about me in that way. I don't think anyone is watching me, or following me, or trying to hurt me at all. 

It's honestly just the discrepancies with my dad's records, nothing else. I just go to work, do my job, and live a very normal, quiet life, I promise. I would absolutely tell you if I felt unsafe or if I noticed anyone following me. 

Is it okay that it's just this one specific thing I'm worried about? I really don't want you to think my mind is playing tricks on me everywhere else. I'm completely fine otherwise, I swear.
Do you generally trust other people, or is it hard for you to trust most people in your life?

Oh, I generally trust people. I really do. Um, I have a great group of friends, and I get along really well with my team at work. I'm honestly not a cynical person at all, I promise. I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt and see the best in them. 

I know that... well, considering what we were just talking about with my dad's records, it might seem like I'm suspicious of everyone, but that's really not the case. It's just that one specific situation. In my day-to-day life, I trust my friends, my colleagues, my neighbors... I'd hate for you to think I'm just walking around doubting everyone I meet. I really value the relationships I have.

Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I am normally. I hope I'm making sense.
Before your father passed away, had you ever had a belief like this about someone hiding the truth or plotting against you?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I've never... um, I've never thought anything like this before. I really want to assure you of that. I've always been a very grounded, rational person. I mean, my job requires me to be very logical, you know? 

This whole thing... it really just started about nine months ago. It was right after he passed, and I was, you know, just trying to do the responsible thing and sort through all his records and his messages. That's when I started noticing the things I mentioned before. But before that? Never. I've never had any reason to think anyone was hiding anything from me. 

I hope that shows you that this isn't just some... some personality flaw or a habit of mine. It's really just tied to this one specific situation over the last nine months. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure you know I haven't always been this way.
If I showed you clear proof that the records and emails were genuine and that nothing was hidden, would you be able to let go of the belief that someone concealed the truth?

Um... wow, that's a... that's a tough question. I really want to say yes. I mean, I know how much easier it would be for everyone if I just... let it go. And I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. I hear them, I really do. 

But... well, I hope you won't be disappointed in me for saying this, but it's just so hard to ignore what I'm seeing. When I sit down and really look at the timestamps, and I see those missing attachments... and then there's the way certain people in his community just kind of avoid my questions when I ask for clarification... it just feels so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

I don't mean to be stubborn, I promise. I really want to be cooperative. It's just... even if you showed me proof, I think part of me would still wonder if it was somehow manipulated, just because of all those little details that don't add up. Is that okay to admit? I really don't want you to think I'm just being difficult or unreasonable. I'm just trying to be honest about how my brain is processing all this.
Before your father passed away, were you generally comfortable with close relationships and emotional closeness, or have you usually preferred to keep other people at a distance?

Oh, I'm definitely comfortable with close relationships. I really don't keep people at a distance at all. I mean, I have a really solid group of friends, and I was very, very close to my dad... which is probably why all of this has been so hard on me. 

But yeah, I've always valued emotional closeness. I've had long-term relationships, and I always try to be a good, supportive partner and friend. I really like being there for the people I care about. I'm definitely not a loner or anything like that, I promise. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, I just want to make sure you know I'm a pretty normal, social guy. I'd hate for you to think I'm isolated or pushing people away, because that's really not me. Did I answer that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Has your belief that someone hid the truth about your father’s death ever changed at all since it started, or has it stayed the same the whole time?

Well, um... I really want to say that it's gotten better, or that I've been able to let it go a little bit. I know that would probably be the best answer, and I really have tried to listen when everyone tells me the hospital records and the donation emails line up perfectly. I really do try to take that in.

But... if I'm being completely honest—and I hope it's okay to just be honest with you—it hasn't really changed. It's stayed pretty much the same the whole time. It's just... whenever I try to put it to rest, I end up looking at those timestamps again, or I notice the missing attachments, or I think about how those people in his community just dodge my questions. It just brings me right back to feeling like it's obvious someone is hiding the truth about what happened. 

I'm really sorry if that's not what you were hoping to hear. I know it probably sounds like I'm not making progress, but I just can't seem to shake it when the details are right there in front of me. Is it normal to get stuck on things like that? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you the truth.
Before your father passed away, did you often feel that other people were untrustworthy or had hidden motives?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've always been a pretty trusting person, I think. I mean, I try to see the best in people, you know? 

Before all this happened with my dad, I never really worried about people having hidden motives or trying to trick me. I've always had good relationships at work and with my friends, and I generally just assume people are being straight with me. I'm definitely not the paranoid type, I promise. 

I know it probably seems like I am right now, because of how stuck I am on the emails and the hospital records... but that's really out of character for me. It's just this one specific situation with my dad that feels so wrong. Usually, I'm very easygoing and trusting. 

Does that make sense? I just really don't want you to think I walk around suspicious of everyone all the time, because that's honestly not who I am at all.
Have you had any experiences of hearing, seeing, or otherwise perceiving things that other people around you do not seem to notice?

No, no, I've never had anything like that happen. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, I promise. 

I know sometimes people who get really focused on things can have those kinds of experiences, and I want to be completely upfront with you, but my mind is totally clear in that way. I'm just a regular guy who is trying to figure out what happened with my dad's estate and the hospital paperwork. I'm not... you know, hallucinating or anything. 

I really hope that's reassuring? I just want to make sure you know I'm completely grounded in reality, except for just being a little too focused on these documents. I'm doing okay on that front, right?
Has this belief about your father’s death been present continuously for at least one month?

Well, um... yes, it has. I guess it's been a while now. It started about nine months ago, right around the time I was trying to sort through his estate and, you know, going through all his records and messages. 

I know nine months sounds like a really long time to be hung up on something like this, and I feel a little embarrassed admitting it's been going on for that long. I really have tried to just put it away and move on, I promise. It's just that every time I think I'm done, I remember a detail that doesn't fit. 

I hope you don't think less of me for not being able to let it go faster. I know most people probably would have just accepted it by now. Is it okay that it's taken me this long to try and figure it out? I'm really trying my best to be reasonable about it.
Before this situation with your father, have you often been suspicious that other people might be deceiving or exploiting you?

Um, I know we touched on this a little bit earlier, but... no, definitely not. I've never worried about people trying to exploit me or deceive me. 

In my job—I'm a computer systems analyst—I work with a lot of different people, and you really have to collaborate and trust your team to get things done. I've always just been the kind of guy who takes people at their word. 

I really hope I'm not giving off the impression that I'm generally suspicious of everyone? Because I promise I'm honestly not. It's really just this one very specific situation with my dad's paperwork that I can't quite reconcile. But before that, no, never. I've always been very trusting. Does that help clarify things for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what I'm usually like.
Has this belief about your father’s death caused problems for you at work or in your daily life?

Well, um... not really, no. I mean, I still go to work every day, and I handle all my projects just fine. I pay my bills on time, keep the house clean, you know... my normal routine is completely intact. I promise I'm not letting this take over my whole life or anything. 

I guess... well, if I'm being completely honest, the only place things get a little tense is when I try to bring up my questions about the records with my family, or sometimes with people at the hospital. They get a bit frustrated with me, and I hate causing any friction. I really don't want to be a burden to anyone. 

But as far as my daily functioning goes, I'm doing really well. I'm keeping everything together, I swear. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure you know I'm still handling my responsibilities like a normal, functioning adult. That's important, right?
Before you started worrying about your father’s death, was there a major stressful event or change in your life that could explain when this began?

Um... no, not that I can think of. I mean, obviously, losing my dad was incredibly stressful, and that was a huge change... but before that happened? No, everything was pretty quiet. 

Work was going well, no big moves or relationship drama or anything like that. I was just living my normal life, doing my job, seeing friends... just regular stuff. I really try to keep my life pretty stable and low-stress whenever I can. I like things to be predictable. 

I hope it doesn't seem like I'm hiding anything, because I'm really not. There just wasn't any other big crisis or anything leading up to all this. It was just... his passing, and then trying to sort out the paperwork. Does that make sense? I'm trying to be as thorough as I can for you.
If someone you trusted and the records themselves clearly showed there was no wrongdoing, would you still believe someone hid the truth about your father’s death?

Um, well... I really, really wish I could just let it go. I know it would make everyone a lot happier if I did. And I know you're probably asking because, you know, people keep telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. I hear them, I really do. 

But... I mean, when I sit down and actually look at the timestamps, and I see the missing attachments on those emails, and... well, the way certain people in the community just completely dodge my questions when I ask politely... I just... I can't ignore it. It's so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

I know that probably sounds stubborn, and I really don't want to be difficult. I'm not trying to be unreasonable, I promise. It's just... the details are right there, you know? I hope you can understand why I can't just brush it under the rug. I'm just trying to do right by my dad. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just want to be honest with you.
Since your father died, have you felt persistently sad or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um... no, not really. I mean, of course I was sad when he passed away—anyone would be, right? It's normal to grieve. But I haven't been, like, depressed or anything. 

I still enjoy my life. I still like doing things... I still play video games on the weekends, and I like tinkering with my computer setups. I haven't lost interest in any of that. I'm keeping my spirits up, I really am. I know it's important to stay positive and keep moving forward, so I make sure to do that. 

I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all day, because I'm definitely not. I'm coping really well, all things considered. That's what you're looking for, right? I'm doing okay emotionally.
If you were shown very clear evidence that nothing unusual happened with your father’s death, would you be able to completely let go of that belief?

Um... I really, really want to say yes to that. I know that's probably the answer you're hoping for, and I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or push back against you. I know I kind of just touched on this, and I really hope you're not getting frustrated with me for repeating myself. 

But... it's just really hard for me to imagine letting it go, because in my mind, I *have* looked at the evidence. When I analyze the data myself—you know, looking closely at the timestamps on those hospital logs, and seeing the specific attachments that were stripped out of the emails—it just... it completely contradicts what everyone is telling me. And then when you add in how people in the community get so quiet and just avoid my questions entirely... I just can't unsee all of that. 

I really wish I could just agree with you and move on, I honestly do. It would make my life, and probably everyone else's, a lot easier. I'm sorry if that makes me seem uncooperative. I'm just trying to be as honest with you as possible about where my head is at. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this? I really just want to make sure I'm doing a good job explaining things for you.
